title: The Sukerchakia misl
hookLine: Charat Singh and Maha Singh's misl, home of the future Maharaja

lines: NOT ONE OF THE BIG MISLS.
cards: Sukarchak was a village. Not a city, not a fort, not a place with a well-known shrine. Tradition places it in the plains north of Lahore, near Gujranwala.
A Sikh named Charat Singh came from there, and the band that gathered round him took the village's name. In the way Sikh histories tell it, it wasn't one of the big misls.
Nobody watching those riders would have guessed what their chief's grandson would become. Today: the Sukerchakia misl.

teach.b: Three generations. First, Charat Singh. Tradition says he was a bold, restless chief who built up his band from a small start, raised a fort at Gujranwala, and fought alongside the other misls in the Dal Khalsa.
He made the Sukerchakias a band other chiefs had to count. Second, his son, Maha Singh.

Tradition says he took up the band young, after his father's death, and carried it further: more villages, more riders, more alliances. It was Maha Singh's son who was promised in marriage to Sada Kaur's daughter.
A small misl was now tied to a strong one. Third, a boy named Ranjit Singh.

He'll have his own days on this path, so only this today: the Maharaja of the Punjab, who would one day rule from Lahore, came out of the Sukerchakia band. Nothing about the beginning looked like a kingdom.
A village name. A chief with a fort. A son who kept going.
And the riders didn't know the ending.
Tradition says neither Charat Singh nor Maha Singh lived to see the boy rule from Lahore.
Each did the next thing with the band he had, and the next generation started a little further on.
A beginning's size doesn't settle where it goes.
The Sukerchakias show what small beginnings look like from the inside.

how: Sikhs meet the Sukerchakia misl in Sikh histories as the band of Charat Singh and Maha Singh, from which Maharaja Ranjit Singh came.

games.q: you're Maha Singh. your father's band is small but growing. a strong misl's leader offers her daughter in marriage to your son. what do you do?
o: refuse; your band should stand alone.
accept, and tie your band to hers.
hand your band over to her.
games.why: the marriage was arranged, and in the way Sikh histories tell it, Sada Kaur later helped the young Ranjit Singh rise.

practice: Bring to mind one thing in your life that started tiny: a friendship that began with one conversation, a habit, a plant, a skill you once fumbled. Remember its very first day, how small it was, then notice where it is now.
If you pray, say Waheguru on each breath out as you stay with that first step.

wordCard.voice: Sukarchak, the village Charat Singh came from, which gave the Sukerchakia misl its name; carried further by Maha Singh, it's the band from which the future Maharaja came. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for maharaja, great king: the title the Sukerchakia boy would one day hold.

carryVoice: Your line: small beginnings. Nobody in the band knew how it would end. See you tomorrow.
